sections.html:
The PVA and the sheriff both work out of the Rowan County Courthouse at 600 West Main Street in Morehead, weekdays 8 AM to 4 PM. The PVA, (606) 784-5512, assesses all taxable real and personal property, tracks ownership changes, keeps parcel maps and handles exemptions. The sheriff, (606) 784-5446, mails and collects the bills.

At the sheriff's window you can pay with cash, a check or a money order. Cards go through an outside vendor that charges 2.49 percent on amounts above $60 and a flat $1.50 on anything smaller. Anyone with a bill number handy can also pay online through the county's property tax page.

Once a bill turns delinquent, the County Clerk and the County Attorney take over from the sheriff. The county's delinquent taxes page describes how the three offices fit together.

Rowan County's discount window runs later than the usual November 1 cutoff and closes on November 30. Bills go out at the start of November.

Rowan County sheriff: what applies at each stage
StageWhat applies
Before November 302 percent discount
By December 31Face amount of the bill
January 1 to January 315 percent penalty
February 1 to April 1521 percent total penalty
After April 15Delinquent, handed to the County Clerk

When a mailing runs late, the Department of Revenue can shift the calendar under KRS 134.015, so dates may move from year to year. The debt attaches to whoever held title on January 1, so a spring seller should plan to settle that year's bill.

sections.h2: Rowan County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Morehead is the seat and Lakeview Heights is the other city. Morehead State University and Cave Run Lake bring steady activity, and part of the Daniel Boone National Forest lies inside the county line. July 2025 population was estimated at 24,476, which is 0.7 percent under 2020. Owners live in 61.5 percent of homes across 9,592 households. A typical home is valued at $161,800 and typical gross rent is $825.

New construction is thin, with eight building permits in 2025, so most listings are existing houses. Because under two thirds of homes are owner-occupied, many parcels are rentals, and a landlord who sells will be asked who covers the year's bill.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and the state rate
sections.html:
The state set its 2025 real estate rate at 10.6 cents per hundred dollars of assessment. Other taxing bodies stack their rates on it, and the sheriff can quote a combined figure for any address.

The deduction matters most for older owners on fixed incomes, and it does not carry over to a buyer. If you sell, the new owner has to file a claim of their own, so mention it during the closing conversation.

Owners from age 65, and owners who are totally disabled, can subtract $49,100 across 2025 and 2026. Apply with the PVA at the courthouse and bring a license or passport.

sections.h2: How Rowan County pursues delinquent taxes
sections.html:
After April 15 the bill rests with the County Clerk, and the county attorney follows a published timetable. Two letters go out on set dates, and the sale usually lands in mid August.

  • May 15: the County Attorney mails a 30-day notice.
  • June 15: a 60-day notice follows for bills still open.
  • Second week of August: the customary sale, where outside investors may buy a bill and add fees.
  • Each month: the delinquent amount climbs by 1 percent until it is paid.

The owner of record can sign a delinquent tax contract with the County Attorney's office up to three days before the sale. The county requires 10 percent of the bill that day and spreads the rest over monthly payments. A contract signed ahead of the clerk's sale keeps investors from buying the bill.

The County Attorney also presses the county's tax claim in foreclosure cases, where it holds priority.

The first step is a required sit-down with the PVA or a deputy. The roll is open for inspection for thirteen days beginning May's first Monday, with the dates and appeal instructions advertised in the county's largest newspaper. At the sit-down the PVA explains how your figure was built and writes it up.

  • File the appeal with the clerk on the workday after viewing ends.
  • Prepare evidence: land and building descriptions, policies, construction costs, listings or sales. A case without any is rejected.
  • The hearing comes roughly a month after viewing, before a panel of local owners.
  • A hired agent must come from a statutory group, among them attorneys, CPAs and appraisers.

Bills printed before a ruling use your claimed value, and a supplemental bill follows if the board lands higher.

sections.h2: Does selling a Rowan County house clear back taxes?
sections.html:
It does not. KRS 134.420 puts a lien on the parcel once taxes turn delinquent, and the lien lasts eleven years under any owner. A title search at the County Clerk reveals it, and it is normally paid off at closing.

Debt grows fast after April 15, because interest, the clerk's commission and the county attorney's fees all join the bill. Paying the sheriff on time avoids that.

An owner who is behind has three routes before the August sale: pay the sheriff, pay the clerk, or sign a contract with the County Attorney. A direct cash sale is a fourth when repairs or inherited debts stand in the way, with the balance taken out of the proceeds.

Gather the paperwork before you list. A current bill, proof that prior years are paid and a copy of your deed answer most buyer questions. Here is a simple order to follow.

  1. Call the sheriff at (606) 784-5446 and confirm the current year shows paid or open.
  2. If any year is behind, ask for a payoff before April 15, or from the County Clerk after that date.
  3. Check with the clerk for any lien recorded against the parcel.
  4. Hand the payoff figure to the closing agent so the debt is paid from your proceeds.
  5. Decide in the contract who pays the current year's bill, since it follows the January 1 owner.

If the house is a rental, tell the buyer's side early which tenant, if any, stays after closing. The year's bill and any lien get sorted out in the same meeting, so it helps to have the lease and the tax paperwork on one desk.

Owners who inherited a house should also bring whatever shows who holds title now. The sheriff and the clerk will only deal with the owner of record, and a payoff quote cannot be finalized until the records match the person signing.

faqs.q: When does the Rowan County discount end?
faqs.a: The county lists a 2 percent discount for bills paid before November 30. The printed amount is then due through December 31, and 5 percent is added in January.

faqs.q: Can I pay the Rowan County sheriff by card?
faqs.a: Yes: Visa, MasterCard, American Express and Discover, through a vendor that charges 2.49 percent above $60 or $1.50 below it. Cash, checks and money orders are welcome too.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Rowan County sheriff's office?
faqs.a: Call (606) 784-5446 or visit 600 West Main Street in Morehead, weekdays 8 AM to 4 PM.

faqs.q: Is a payment plan possible once a Rowan County bill is delinquent?
faqs.a: Yes, through the County Attorney's office: 10 percent of the bill is due on signing day and the remainder is split into monthly payments. Sign before the sale to keep investors out.

faqs.q: Who handles questions about a Rowan County valuation?
faqs.a: The Property Valuation Administrator, at (606) 784-5512. A conference there comes before any appeal at the County Clerk.
